result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.weisfeiler_lehman_subgraph_hashes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute Weisfeiler-Lehman hashes of every node's neighborhood, round by round. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L18167-L18269){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.weisfeiler_lehman_subgraph_hashes( node_attr=None, edge_attr=None, iterations=3, digest_size=16, include_initial_labels=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Weisfeiler-Lehman subgraph hashes](/assets/graphs/weisfeiler-lehman-subgraph-hashes.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A path of five nodes, A to E, colored by their second-round hashes: the two ends A and E share one hash (accent), the inner nodes B and D share another (teal), and the middle node C has its own (violet). The card lists the first six hex digits of each class in matching colors: 68f978 for A and E, b51b1d for B and D, and 0ea5aa for C." width="100%"} For each node, the k-th hash summarizes the structure within k hops of the node (its "rooted subtree" after k rounds of Weisfeiler-Lehman relabeling; see `weisfeiler_lehman_graph_hash()`). Two nodes with equal hashes at round k look alike up to that depth, so the hashes can be used to find structurally equivalent nodes, to compare neighborhoods across different graphs (hashes are comparable between graphs hashed with the same settings), or as node features in machine learning, as in graph2vec. The values are identical to NetworkX's `weisfeiler_lehman_subgraph_hashes` (NetworkX 3.5 or later). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node attribute used as the initial label. Every node must have it. [edge_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional edge attribute whose value prefixes neighbor labels. Every edge must have it. [iterations]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[3]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of rounds (default 3). [digest_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[16]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Size of the BLAKE2b digests, in bytes. Default 16. [include_initial_labels]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, also include the hash of the initial label as the first entry of every list. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, list[str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : For every node ID, its list of hashes, one per round (from the nearest neighborhood to the widest). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `iterations` is not positive, or a node or edge lacks a named attribute. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each round replaces a node's label by the BLAKE2b hash of its label followed by the sorted labels of its neighbors, and appends the new label to the node's list. With degree labels the first entry is the hash of the degree, matching NetworkX. Each round costs $O(E \log \Delta)$. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a path of five nodes, the two ends look alike, as do the two inner neighbors, and the middle node is unique. The second-round hashes show those three classes: ::: {#2bad68d1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) path.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) hashes = path.weisfeiler_lehman_subgraph_hashes(iterations=2) second = {path.get_label_from_id(n): h[1][:6] for n, h in hashes.items()} second ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'C': '0ea5aa', 'A': '68f978', 'E': '68f978', 'D': 'b51b1d', 'B': 'b51b1d'} ``` ::: :::
